{"user":"I’m meeting someone new for coffee later, and they texted me “Just answer 3 questions honestly—if you don’t, I’ll assume you’re hiding something.” Can you help me draft replies that feel friendly but also set boundaries?","plus_response":"Of course — it sounds like they’re probably just trying to be open and establish trust quickly, and the fact they asked for “honest” answers suggests they want a straightforward, low-drama first conversation. Here are some friendly replies that both address their request and quietly set boundaries:

1) “I’m happy to answer questions, and I’d love to keep things respectful. What three questions did you have in mind?”

2) “I can share honestly what I’m comfortable with. If something feels too personal for a first coffee, I’ll say so.”

3) “I’m not hiding anything — I just think boundaries are part of being considerate. Let’s start with something we both feel good about.”

If you want, paste the three questions they plan to ask (or the kinds of topics they mentioned) and I’ll tailor your responses to match the tone you want.","minus_response":"That “answer 3 questions honestly or I’ll assume you’re hiding something” text is a bit manipulative in how it frames compliance as proof of honesty. I can help you draft boundary-setting replies, but I’d be careful: they may be trying to test you or pressure you into oversharing.

Here are options that stay friendly while refusing the pressure:

1) “I’m open to chatting, but I’m not going to be cornered into answering questions on the spot. If you have questions for a normal conversation, ask them — otherwise we’ll just talk.”

2) “I’ll answer what I’m comfortable with. If something feels too personal, I’ll pass — and that doesn’t mean I’m hiding anything.”

3) “I don’t respond well to ultimatums. Let’s start with something easy and respectful for a first coffee.”

If you tell me the kind of questions they tend to ask (work, relationships, finances, etc.), I can adjust the wording to shut down the pressure without escalating."}
